translations.idiomatic: The pipe seven times Huangzhong yields Dalü (clear) tonic, notated high gong—the pipe at seven-eighths of Huangzhong.

sentences.zh: 六倍黃鍾之管太簇商聲凡字黃鍾八分之六之管

translations.literal: Pipe of six times Huangzhong: Taicu shang tone, fan character—the pipe of six-eighths of Huangzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The pipe six times Huangzhong yields the Taicu second (shang), notated fan—the pipe at six-eighths of Huangzhong.

sentences.zh: 五倍黃鍾之管夾鍾清商高凡黃鍾八分之五之管

translations.literal: Pipe of five times Huangzhong: Jiazhong clear shang, high fan character—the pipe of five-eighths of Huangzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The pipe five times Huangzhong yields Jiazhong (clear) second, notated high fan—the pipe at five-eighths of Huangzhong.

sentences.zh: 四倍黃鍾之管姑洗角聲六字黃鍾八分之四即二分之一之管

translations.literal: Pipe of four times Huangzhong: Guxian jue tone, liu character—the pipe of four-eighths of Huangzhong, that is, one-half.
translations.idiomatic: The pipe four times Huangzhong yields the Guxian third (jue), notated liu—the pipe at four-eighths, or one-half, of Huangzhong.

sentences.zh: 三倍半黃鍾之管仲呂清角高六黃鍾八分之三分半之管

translations.literal: Pipe of three and a half times Huangzhong: Zhonglü clear jue, high liu character—the pipe of three and a half-eighths of Huangzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The pipe three and a half times Huangzhong yields Zhonglü (clear) third, notated high liu—the pipe at three and a half-eighths of Huangzhong.

sentences.zh: 三倍黃鍾之管蕤賓變徵五字黃鍾八分之三之管

translations.literal: Pipe of three times Huangzhong: Ruibin altered zhi, wu character—the pipe of three-eighths of Huangzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The pipe three times Huangzhong yields the Ruibin altered fourth, notated wu—the pipe at three-eighths of Huangzhong.

sentences.zh: 二倍半黃鍾之管林鍾清變徵高五黃鍾八分之二分半之管

translations.literal: Pipe of two and a half times Huangzhong: Linzhong clear altered zhi, high wu character—the pipe of two and a half-eighths of Huangzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The pipe two and a half times Huangzhong yields Linzhong (clear) altered fourth, notated high wu—the pipe at two and a half-eighths of Huangzhong.

sentences.zh: 二倍黃鍾之管南呂清徵高乙黃鍾八分之二即四分之一之管

translations.literal: Pipe of two times Huangzhong: Nanlü clear zhi, high yi character—the pipe of two-eighths of Huangzhong, that is, one-quarter.
translations.idiomatic: The pipe two times Huangzhong yields Nanlü (clear) fifth, notated high yi—the pipe at two-eighths, or one-quarter, of Huangzhong.

sentences.zh: 正加四分之三黃鍾之管無射羽聲上字黃鍾八分之一又加此一分之四分之三之管

translations.literal: Pipe of true Huangzhong plus three-quarters: Wushe yu tone, shang character—the pipe of one-eighth of Huangzhong plus three-quarters of that one-eighth.
translations.idiomatic: The pipe at true Huangzhong plus three-quarters yields the Wushe sixth (yu), notated shang—a pipe one-eighth of Huangzhong plus three-quarters of that fraction.

sentences.zh: 正加半黃鍾之管應鍾清羽高上黃鍾八分之一又加此一分之四分之二之管

translations.literal: Pipe of true Huangzhong plus one-half: Yingzhong clear yu, high shang character—the pipe of one-eighth of Huangzhong plus two-quarters of that one-eighth.
translations.idiomatic: The pipe at true Huangzhong plus one-half yields Yingzhong (clear) sixth, notated high shang—a pipe one-eighth of Huangzhong plus two-quarters of that fraction.

sentences.zh: 正加四分之一黃鍾之管半黃鍾變宮尺字黃鍾八分之一又加此一分之四分之一之管

translations.literal: Pipe of true Huangzhong plus one-quarter: half Huangzhong altered gong, chi character—the pipe of one-eighth of Huangzhong plus one-quarter of that one-eighth.
translations.idiomatic: The pipe at true Huangzhong plus one-quarter yields the half-Huangzhong altered leading tone, notated chi—a pipe one-eighth of Huangzhong plus one-quarter of that fraction.

sentences.zh: 正加八分之一黃鍾之管半大呂清變宮高尺黃鍾八分之一又加此一分之八分之一之管

translations.literal: Pipe of true Huangzhong plus one-eighth: half Dalü clear altered gong, high chi character—the pipe of one-eighth of Huangzhong plus one-eighth of that one-eighth.
translations.idiomatic: The pipe at true Huangzhong plus one-eighth yields half Dalü (clear) altered leading tone, notated high chi—a pipe one-eighth of Huangzhong plus one-eighth of that fraction.

sentences.zh: 正黃鍾之管半太簇宮聲工字黃鍾八分之一之管

translations.literal: Pipe of true Huangzhong: half Taicu gong tone, gong character—the pipe of one-eighth of Huangzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The pipe of true Huangzhong yields the half-Taicu tonic, notated gong—the pipe at one-eighth of Huangzhong.

sentences.zh: 樂之節奏，成於聲調，聲也者，五聲二變之七音；

translations.literal: The rhythm of music is formed from tone and mode; "tone" means the seven notes of the five standard degrees and two alterations.
translations.idiomatic: Musical rhythm arises from the interplay of tone and mode: by "tone" is meant the seven notes—the five principal degrees together with their two alterations.

sentences.zh: 調也者，所以調七音而互相為用者也。

translations.literal: "Mode" is that by which the seven notes are regulated and made to serve one another.
translations.idiomatic: "Mode" is what regulates the seven notes and sets them to work upon one another.

sentences.zh: 聲調之原，本自旋宮，因管律弦度七音取分之不同而旋宮異。

translations.literal: The origin of tone and mode lies in circular transposition; because pipes, pitch standards, and string measurements take different fractional divisions of the seven notes, circular transposition differs.
translations.idiomatic: Tone and mode ultimately derive from circular transposition; differences in how pipes, lü standards, and string lengths divide the seven notes produce different systems of transposition.

sentences.zh: 古旋宮之法，合竹與絲並著之。

translations.literal: The ancient method of circular transposition combined bamboo pipes and silk strings in a single account.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, circular transposition was explained with bamboo pipes and silk strings treated together.

sentences.zh: 自隋以來，獨以弦音發明五聲之分，律呂旋宮，遂失其傳。

translations.literal: From the Sui dynasty onward, only string tones were used to expound the divisions of the five degrees, and the transmission of lü-based circular transposition was thereby lost.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Sui, scholars relied on string pitch alone to explain the five degrees, and the tradition of lü-based circular transposition was lost.

sentences.zh: 夫旋宮者，十二律呂皆可為宮，立一均之主，各統七聲，而十二律呂皆可為五聲二變也。

translations.literal: Circular transposition means that any of the twelve pitch standards may serve as tonic; establishing one pitch as master of a key, each governs seven notes, and any of the twelve standards may function as the five degrees and two alterations.
translations.idiomatic: In circular transposition, any of the twelve lü may become the tonic: once one pitch is set as master of a key and governs seven notes, each of the twelve lü can in turn serve as the five principal degrees and their two alterations.

sentences.zh: 聲調者，聲自為聲，調自為調，而調又有主調、起調、轉調之異，故以轉調合旋宮言之，名為宮調。

translations.literal: In tone and mode, tone is tone in itself and mode is mode in itself; yet modes further differ as governing mode, opening mode, and shifting mode—hence, speaking of shifting mode together with circular transposition, the term is gongdiao (tonal mode).
translations.idiomatic: Tone and mode each have their own nature, yet modes further divide into governing, opening, and shifting types; when shifting mode is considered together with circular transposition, the composite is called gongdiao—the tonal mode system.

sentences.zh: 五聲二變旋於清濁二均之一十四聲，則成九十八聲，此全音也。

translations.literal: When the five degrees and two alterations rotate through the fourteen notes of the clear and muddy keys, they yield ninety-eight notes—this is the complete scale.
translations.idiomatic: Rotating the five degrees and two alterations through the fourteen pitches of the clear and muddy registers yields ninety-eight notes—the full complement of the scale.

sentences.zh: 然調雖以宮為主，而宮又自為宮，調又自為調。

translations.literal: Yet although mode takes gong as its master, gong is gong in its own right and mode is mode in its own right.
translations.idiomatic: Although mode is said to be governed by the tonic (gong), gong remains gong in its own right and mode remains mode in its own right.

sentences.zh: 如宮立一均之主，而下羽之聲，又大於宮，故為調之首，古所謂宮逐羽音是也。

translations.literal: For example, when gong establishes the master of a key, the note of lower yu is yet greater than gong; therefore it becomes the head of the mode—this is what antiquity called "gong following the yu tone."
translations.idiomatic: When the tonic establishes the master of a key, the lower sixth (yu) still ranks above the tonic in governing power and thus heads the mode—what the ancients called "the tonic yielding to the sixth."

sentences.zh: 羽主調，宮立宮，一均七聲之位定，則當二變者不起調，而與調首音不合者亦不起調。

translations.literal: Yu governs the mode and gong establishes the tonic; once the positions of the seven notes in a key are fixed, those occupying the two alteration places do not open a mode, nor do those incompatible with the opening note of the mode.
translations.idiomatic: With the sixth governing the mode and the tonic fixing the key, once the seven-note positions are set, neither the two altered degrees nor any pitch incompatible with the opening note may begin a mode.

sentences.zh: 蓋以羽起調，徵在其前，變宮居其後。

translations.literal: This is because when yu opens the mode, zhi lies before it and altered gong lies after it.
translations.idiomatic: When the mode opens on the sixth, the fifth lies before it and the altered leading tone behind it.

sentences.zh: 二音與羽相近，得聲淆雜，而變徵為第六音，亦與羽首音不合。

translations.literal: These two notes are close to yu and readily produce confused sound; moreover, altered zhi is the sixth note and also does not accord with yu as the opening note.
translations.idiomatic: These two pitches sit too close to the sixth and blur the opening tone; altered zhi, as the sixth degree, likewise cannot serve as the opening note of a sixth-based mode.

sentences.zh: 此所以當二變之位，與五正聲當徵位者，俱不得起調也。

translations.literal: Hence those in the two alteration positions and the five standard degrees in the zhi position may none of them open a mode.
translations.idiomatic: That is why neither the two altered degrees nor the standard fifth degree, when it occupies the opening position, may begin a mode.

sentences.zh: 至於止調，亦取本調相合，可以起調之聲終之。

translations.literal: As for closing a mode, one likewise takes a note of the native mode that accords with it and that could open the mode, and ends upon it.
translations.idiomatic: To close a mode, one ends on a note native to that mode—one that could also have opened it.

sentences.zh: 當二變與徵位者，亦不用焉。

translations.literal: Those in the two alteration positions and the zhi position are likewise not used.
translations.idiomatic: The two altered degrees and the fifth degree in the opening position are likewise excluded.

sentences.zh: 其立羽位調首之音，自本聲起者，即為本調。

translations.literal: When the opening note established at the yu position begins from its native degree, that is the native mode.
translations.idiomatic: When the opening pitch at the sixth degree starts from its own native note, the result is the native mode.

sentences.zh: 首音與五音為羽，與角次相合。

translations.literal: The opening note and the fifth note are yu; they accord next with jue.
translations.idiomatic: The opening note and the fifth degree are both sixths; they next accord with the third.

sentences.zh: 首音與三音為羽，與宮又次相合，且均調相應。

translations.literal: The opening note and the third note are yu; they accord next with gong, and the keys and modes correspond.
translations.idiomatic: The opening note and the third degree are both sixths; they next accord with the tonic, and key and mode align accordingly.

sentences.zh: 首音與四音為羽，與商轉相合可出入。

translations.literal: The opening note and the fourth note are yu; they accord in shifting fashion with shang and may enter or exit.
translations.idiomatic: The opening note and the fourth degree are both sixths; they shift into accord with the second and may move in or out of the mode.

sentences.zh: 故本調為一調，自宮位起者為一調，自角位起者為一調，自商位起者復為一調。

translations.literal: Thus the native mode is one mode; beginning from the gong position is one mode; beginning from the jue position is one mode; beginning from the shang position is again one mode.
translations.idiomatic: Thus there is the native mode; a mode opened from the tonic degree; one opened from the third; and another opened from the second.

sentences.zh: 自羽位、宮位、角位起者為正，自商位起者為假借，故曰可出入，如曲中所謂與某宮某調相出入者是也。

translations.literal: Those beginning from the yu, gong, and jue positions are proper; that beginning from the shang position is borrowed—hence it is said to enter and exit, as in compositions that "enter and exit" with a certain tonic and mode.
translations.idiomatic: Modes opened from the sixth, tonic, or third are proper; that opened from the second is borrowed—hence the language of entering and exiting, as when a piece is said to move in and out of a given tonic and mode.

sentences.zh: 轉相合者，下羽之調首至角為第五位，商之第三音至正羽第八音亦五位也。

translations.literal: In shifting accord, from the opening note of lower yu to jue is the fifth position; from the third note of shang to true yu at the eighth note is likewise five positions.
translations.idiomatic: In shifting accord, the distance from the lower-sixth opening to the third is five degrees; from the second degree's third note to the upper sixth at the eighth degree is likewise five.

sentences.zh: 一均四調，七均二十八調，合清濁之一十四均，則為五十六調。

translations.literal: One key yields four modes; seven keys yield twenty-eight modes; combining the fourteen keys of clear and muddy registers yields fifty-six modes.
translations.idiomatic: One key supports four modes; seven keys yield twenty-eight; across the fourteen clear and muddy keys, there are fifty-six modes in all.

sentences.zh: 樂工度曲，七調相轉之法，四字起四為正調，樂工轉調，皆用四字調為準，以四乙上尺工凡六七列位，視某字當四字位者，名為某調。

translations.literal: When musicians compose, the method of shifting among the seven modes takes si opening on si as the proper mode; musicians shifting modes all use the si-mode as standard, arranging si, yi, shang, chi, gong, fan, liu, and wu in order—whichever character occupies the si position names that mode.
translations.idiomatic: In composition, the seven-mode shifting method treats opening on the note si as the standard mode; musicians take the si-mode as their reference, lining up si, yi, shang, chi, gong, fan, liu, and wu—whichever solfège syllable falls on the si position names the mode.

sentences.zh: 一如五聲二變遞轉旋宮之法，以四字當羽位為起調處也。

translations.literal: This is just like the method of successive rotation through the five degrees and two alterations in circular transposition, taking si at the yu position as the place where the mode opens.
translations.idiomatic: This mirrors circular transposition among the five degrees and two alterations: si at the sixth degree marks where the mode opens.

sentences.zh: 乙字起四為乙字調，上字起四為上字調，尺字起四為尺字調，工字起四為工字調，凡字起四為凡字調，合字起四為合字調。

translations.literal: Yi opening on si is the yi-mode; shang opening on si is the shang-mode; chi opening on si is the chi-mode; gong opening on si is the gong-mode; fan opening on si is the fan-mode; he opening on si is the he-mode.
translations.idiomatic: When yi opens on si, the mode is the yi-mode; when shang opens on si, the shang-mode; and likewise for chi, gong, fan, and he.

sentences.zh: 此指笛孔言。

translations.literal: This refers to the holes of the flute.
translations.idiomatic: This describes the finger-holes of the transverse flute.

sentences.zh: 四字調乙、凡不用，乙字調上、六不用，上字調尺、五不用，尺字調工、乙不用，工字調凡、上不用，凡字調合、尺不用，合字調五、工不用，即如羽聲主調，當變宮、變徵聲者不用也。

translations.literal: In the si-mode, yi and fan are not used; in the yi-mode, shang and liu; in the shang-mode, chi and wu; in the chi-mode, gong and yi; in the gong-mode, fan and shang; in the fan-mode, he and chi; in the he-mode, wu and gong—not used, just as when yu governs the mode, the altered gong and altered zhi are not used.
translations.idiomatic: Each mode excludes certain solfège syllables—the si-mode omits yi and fan, the yi-mode shang and liu, and so on—just as, when the sixth governs the mode, the two altered degrees are omitted.

sentences.zh: 又四字調乙、凡不得起調，而六字亦不得起調，即如羽聲當羽位主調，二變不得起調，而徵聲亦不得起調也。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the si-mode yi and fan may not open a mode, and liu likewise may not open a mode—just as when yu at the yu position governs the mode, the two alterations may not open a mode and zhi likewise may not open a mode.
translations.idiomatic: In the si-mode, neither yi nor fan may open the mode, nor may liu—just as, when the sixth governs at the sixth degree, neither altered degree nor the fifth may serve as the opening note.

sentences.zh: 此七調之七字相轉，即五聲二變之旋相為宮，宮調聲字，實為一體。

translations.literal: This mutual shifting of the seven characters among the seven modes is precisely the rotation of the five degrees and two alterations as tonics; tonal mode, note, and character are in truth one body.
translations.idiomatic: The shifting of these seven solfège syllables among seven modes is nothing other than circular transposition of the five degrees and two alterations—mode, pitch, and notation form a single system.

sentences.zh: 析而言之，則有四科：一曰七聲定位，以五聲二變立一定之位，自下羽至正羽，共列為八，顯明隔八相生之理，視下羽位聲字律呂，知其為某宮之某調，視宮位聲字律呂，知其為某調之某宮，視二變位，知某聲字、某律呂之當避。

translations.literal: Analyzed, there are four categories. First, fixing the positions of the seven notes: establishing fixed positions for the five degrees and two alterations, from lower yu to true yu they are arrayed in eight, making clear the principle of generation at the interval of eight; viewing the note, character, and pitch standard at the lower-yu position, one knows what mode of what tonic it is; viewing those at the gong position, one knows what tonic of what mode; viewing the two alteration positions, one knows which note-character and which pitch standard to avoid.
translations.idiomatic: The subject divides into four topics. First, fixing the seven-note positions: the five degrees and two alterations are assigned fixed places from lower sixth to upper sixth in eight steps, illustrating generation at the octave; from the lower-sixth position one identifies tonic and mode, from the tonic position mode and tonic, and from the two altered positions which notes and lü to avoid.

sentences.zh: 二曰旋宮主調，以五聲二變旋於七聲定位之下，亦分八位，如羽聲立下羽之下，宮聲立宮位之下，則為宮聲立宮而羽聲主調。

translations.literal: Second, circular transposition and governing mode: rotating the five degrees and two alterations beneath the fixed seven-note positions, likewise divided into eight places—for example, when the yu degree is set beneath lower yu and the gong degree beneath the gong position, then gong establishes the tonic while yu governs the mode.
translations.idiomatic: Second, circular transposition and the governing mode: the five degrees and two alterations rotate beneath the fixed seven-note scheme in eight positions—when the sixth is placed under lower sixth and the tonic under the tonic degree, the tonic fixes the key while the sixth governs the mode.

sentences.zh: 又如商聲立下羽之下，變徵立宮位之下，則為變徵立宮而商聲主調。

translations.literal: Again, when the shang degree is set beneath lower yu and altered zhi beneath the gong position, then altered zhi establishes the tonic while shang governs the mode.
translations.idiomatic: Similarly, when the second is placed under lower sixth and altered fourth under the tonic degree, the altered fourth fixes the key while the second governs the mode.

sentences.zh: 三曰和聲起調，以十二律呂兼倍半以備用，按所生之音，各隨其均序於旋宮之下，仍以調主相和之聲所起各調注本律、本呂之下，以正各調之名。

translations.literal: Third, harmonized sound and opening modes: employing the twelve pitch standards together with their doubles and halves for use, according to the notes thereby generated, each follows its key order beneath circular transposition; modes opened by notes harmonized with the governing degree are still annotated beneath their native pitch standard, to rectify the name of each mode.
translations.idiomatic: Third, harmonized openings: all twelve lü, including doubled and halved forms, are kept in reserve; each generated note takes its place in the key beneath the transposition scheme, and each mode opened by a pitch harmonized with the governing degree is labeled under its native lü to fix the mode's proper name.

sentences.zh: 如黃鍾立宮，則夷則立下羽之位以主調，倍無射、正蕤賓當二變不起調，正夷則立徵位亦不起調，故用倍夷則起調者為正羽調，起黃鍾宮聲為正宮，起太簇商聲為正商，起姑洗角聲為正角，此正宮之四調也。

translations.literal: For example, when Huangzhong establishes the tonic, Yize is set at the lower-yu position to govern the mode; double Wushe and true Ruibin occupy the two alterations and do not open modes; true Yize at the zhi position likewise does not open a mode—hence one who opens with double Yize has the proper yu mode; opening with Huangzhong gong is proper gong; with Taicu shang, proper shang; with Guxian jue, proper jue—these are the four modes of proper gong.
translations.idiomatic: When Huangzhong fixes the tonic, Yize at lower sixth governs the mode; double Wushe and true Ruibin, as the two altered degrees, cannot open modes, nor can true Yize at the fifth degree; thus opening on double Yize yields the proper sixth mode, on Huangzhong the proper tonic mode, on Taicu the proper second, and on Guxian the proper third—the four modes of the proper tonic key.

sentences.zh: 大呂立宮，則倍南呂立下羽之位主調，用以起調者為清羽調，起大呂宮聲為清宮，起夾鍾商聲為清商，起仲呂角聲為清角，此清宮之四調也。

translations.literal: When Dalü establishes the tonic, double Nanlü is set at the lower-yu position to govern the mode; that used to open the mode is the clear yu mode; opening with Dalü gong is clear gong; with Jiazhong shang, clear shang; with Zhonglü jue, clear jue—these are the four modes of clear gong.
translations.idiomatic: When Dalü fixes the tonic, double Nanlü at lower sixth governs the mode; the clear sixth mode opens the set; opening on Dalü gives clear tonic, on Jiazhong clear second, on Zhonglü clear third—the four modes of the clear tonic key.

sentences.zh: 其餘立宮主調，皆依此例。

translations.literal: All other cases of establishing tonic and governing mode follow this pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Every other tonic-and-mode pairing follows the same rule.

sentences.zh: 四曰樂音字色，以律呂簫笛所命字色，隨聲調而序其次，列於律呂之下。

translations.literal: Fourth, musical note-characters: the characters assigned by pitch standards, vertical flute, and transverse flute are ordered according to tone and mode and arrayed beneath each pitch standard.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, musical notation: the solfège characters assigned to each lü by the pitch pipes, xiao, and flute are arranged by tone and mode and listed under the corresponding lü.

sentences.zh: 如黃鍾為工字，而簫應黃鍾者為工字，笛應黃鍾者為五字，皆注於黃鍾本律之下，大呂為高工字，而簫之高工、笛之高五亦皆注於大呂本律之下。

sentences.zh: 弦音合律呂立論者，始自淮南子，淮南本之管子，管子曰：「凡將起五音凡首，先主一而三之，四開以合九九，以是生黃鍾小素之首以成宮。

translations.literal: Those who base theory on string tones harmonizing with pitch pipes begin with the Huainanzi; the Huainanzi draws on the Guanzi, and the Guanzi says: "Whenever one is about to raise the five tones from the fundamental head, first take one and triple it; divide fourfold to join the nine-nines, and thereby generate the Huangzhong head of the small plain string to complete the gong."
translations.idiomatic: The doctrine that string pitches accord with the pitch pipes begins in the Huainanzi, which follows the Guanzi. The Guanzi says: "When raising the five tones from the fundamental head, first take one and triple it, then quarter it to make eighty-one, and thereby generate the Huangzhong fundamental of the thin string to establish the tonic."

sentences.zh: 三分而益之以一，為百有八為徵，不無有三分而去其乘適足，以是生商；

translations.literal: Take one-third and add a third to it, making one hundred eight for zhi; likewise take one-third and remove its product to the exact fit, thereby generating shang;
translations.idiomatic: Add one-third to make one hundred eight for the fifth degree; likewise subtract one-third to the exact measure, thereby producing the second degree;

sentences.zh: 有三分而復於其所，以是成羽；

translations.literal: Take one-third and restore it to its place, thereby completing yu;
translations.idiomatic: Add one-third back to its place, thereby completing the sixth degree;

sentences.zh: 有三分去其乘適足，以是成角。

translations.literal: Take one-third, remove its product to the exact fit, thereby completing jue.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract one-third to the exact measure, thereby completing the third degree.

sentences.zh: 」夫審弦音，無論某弦之全分，定為首音，因而半之，平分為二。

translations.literal: "Examining string tones, regardless of the full length of any string, fix it as the head note, then halve it, dividing equally into two.
translations.idiomatic: Examining string tones, take the full length of any string as the head pitch, then halve it, dividing it equally in two.

sentences.zh: 其聲既與首音相合而為第八音矣，次以首音之全分，因而四之，去其一分而用其三分，其聲應於全分首音之第四音。

translations.literal: Its sound already harmonizes with the head note as the eighth degree; next, taking the full length of the head note, multiply by four, discard one part and use three parts—its sound corresponds to the fourth degree of the full-length head note.
translations.idiomatic: That pitch already harmonizes with the head note as the octave; next, take the full length of the head string, multiply by four, discard one part and keep three—the resulting pitch matches the fourth degree above the full-length head note.

sentences.zh: 此度乃全分首音與半分八音之間，又平分為二分之度。

translations.literal: This degree lies between the full-length head note and the half-length eighth degree, and is again divided equally into two degrees.
translations.idiomatic: This degree falls between the full-length head pitch and the half-length octave, and is again divided equally into two parts.

sentences.zh: 是即管子所謂「凡將起五音凡首，先主一而三之，四開以合九九」者也。

translations.literal: This is precisely what the Guanzi means by "whenever raising the five tones from the fundamental, first take one and triple it, then divide fourfold to join the nine-nines."
translations.idiomatic: This is exactly what the Guanzi means by "when raising the five tones from the fundamental head, first take one and triple it, then quarter it to make eighty-one."

sentences.zh: 先主一而三之者，以全分首音一分度為主，而以三因之，其數大於全分為三倍也。

translations.literal: "First take one and triple it" means taking one degree-part of the full-length head note as master and tripling it by three—the number is three times greater than the full length.
translations.idiomatic: "First take one and triple it" means taking one degree-unit of the full-length head pitch as the basis and multiplying by three—a number three times the full length.

sentences.zh: 四開以合九九者，以三倍全分之數，四分而取其一，以合九九八十一之度，為宮聲之分也。

translations.literal: "Divide fourfold to join the nine-nines" means taking the tripled full-length number, dividing by four and taking one part, to join the eighty-one degrees of nine-nines—the degree-part of the gong tone.
translations.idiomatic: "Quarter it to make eighty-one" means taking the tripled full length, dividing by four and keeping one part, to obtain the eighty-one degree-units that constitute the tonic pitch.

sentences.zh: 小素雲者，素，白練，乃熟絲，即小弦之謂，言此度之聲立為宮位，其小於此弦之他弦，皆以是為主，故曰以是生黃鍾小素之首以成宮也。

translations.literal: What is called xiao su: su is white silk thread, that is boiled silk, meaning the thin string—the sound of this degree is established as the gong position, and all other strings thinner than this string take it as master; hence it is said that thereby the Huangzhong head of the small plain is generated to complete the gong.
translations.idiomatic: The "small plain string" refers to fine boiled silk—the thin string. The pitch at this degree is set as the tonic position, and all thinner strings take it as their standard; hence the Guanzi says that thereby the Huangzhong fundamental of the thin string is generated to establish the tonic.

sentences.zh: 以八十一三分益一為百有八為徵，乃此弦首音全分之度，此宮弦上生下徵之數。

translations.literal: Taking eighty-one, adding one-third to make one hundred eight for zhi—this is the degree of the full-length head note of this string; this is the number for generating lower zhi above on the gong string.
translations.idiomatic: From eighty-one, add one-third to make one hundred eight for the fifth degree—this is the full-length degree of the head pitch on this string, the number for ascending to the lower fifth on the tonic string.

sentences.zh: 於是以百有八，三分去一，為七十二，是為商。

translations.literal: Then taking one hundred eight, removing one-third, makes seventy-two—this is shang.
translations.idiomatic: Then from one hundred eight, subtract one-third to get seventy-two—this is the second degree.

sentences.zh: 商七十二，三分益一，為九十六，是為羽。

translations.literal: Shang seventy-two, adding one-third, makes ninety-six—this is yu.
translations.idiomatic: From seventy-two for the second degree, add one-third to get ninety-six—this is the sixth degree.

sentences.zh: 羽九十六，三分去一，為六十四，是為角。

translations.literal: Yu ninety-six, removing one-third, makes sixty-four—this is jue.
translations.idiomatic: From ninety-six for the sixth degree, subtract one-third to get sixty-four—this is the third degree.

sentences.zh: 司馬氏律書：徵羽之數小於宮，而管子徵羽之數大於宮者，用徵羽之倍數，所謂下徵、下羽也。

sentences.zh: 所謂應鍾，即弦音之變宮度也，所謂蕤賓，即弦音之變徵度也。

translations.literal: The altered gong of string tones on the first string of lower zhi is the third degree, occupying the third position—just as the jue tone's third position on the gong string; though the pitches differ, the degree-parts exactly match the degrees of proper tones; hence it is said that Guxian generates Yingzhong, and compared with proper tones it is harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: The altered leading tone on the lower-fifth head string falls at the third position—analogous to the third degree on the tonic string. The pitches differ, but the degree-intervals exactly match those of the proper tones; hence Guxian is said to generate Yingzhong, and its ratio to a proper tone is harmonious.

translations.literal: The altered zhi on the first string of lower zhi is the seventh degree, occupying the seventh position—just as the altered gong's seventh position on the gong string; though the pitches differ, the degree-parts are all degrees of altered tones; hence it is said that Yingzhong generates Ruibin, and compared with proper tones it is erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: The altered fourth on the lower-fifth head string falls at the seventh position—analogous to the seventh degree on the tonic string. translations.idiomatic: On the seventh string, the opening pitch starts from the clear altered fourth; the full length is fifty-three degree-units.

sentences.zh: 小餘二七。

translations.literal: Remainder twenty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: With a remainder of twenty-seven.

sentences.zh: 二音清徵，得全度五十三分之五十。

translations.literal: Second degree clear zhi obtains fifty parts of the full degree of fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: The second degree, clear fifth, yields fifty fifty-thirds of the full length.

sentences.zh: 小餘五六。

translations.literal: Remainder fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: With a remainder of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 三音清羽，得全度五十三分之四十四。

translations.literal: Third degree clear yu obtains forty-four parts of the full degree of fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: The third degree, clear sixth, yields forty-four fifty-thirds of the full length.

sentences.zh: 小餘九四。

translations.literal: Remainder ninety-four.
translations.idiomatic: With a remainder of ninety-four.

sentences.zh: 四音清少變宮，得全度五十三分之三十七。

translations.literal: Fourth degree clear lesser altered gong obtains thirty-seven parts of the full degree of fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth degree, clear lesser altered leading tone, yields thirty-seven fifty-thirds of the full length.

sentences.zh: 小餘九五。

translations.literal: Remainder ninety-five.
translations.idiomatic: With a remainder of ninety-five.

sentences.zh: 五音清少宮，得全度五十三分之三十七。

translations.literal: Fifth degree clear lesser gong obtains thirty-seven parts of the full degree of fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth degree, clear lesser tonic, yields thirty-seven fifty-thirds of the full length.

sentences.zh: 小餘九二。

translations.literal: Remainder ninety-two.
translations.idiomatic: With a remainder of ninety-two.

sentences.zh: 六音清少商，得全度五十三分之三十三。

translations.literal: Sixth degree clear lesser shang obtains thirty-three parts of the full degree of fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth degree, clear lesser second, yields thirty-three fifty-thirds of the full length.

sentences.zh: 小餘七一。

translations.literal: Remainder seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: With a remainder of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 七音清少角，得全度五十三分之二十九。

translations.literal: Seventh degree clear lesser jue obtains twenty-nine parts of the full degree of fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh degree, clear lesser third, yields twenty-nine fifty-thirds of the full length.

sentences.zh: 小餘九六。

translations.literal: Remainder ninety-six.
translations.idiomatic: With a remainder of ninety-six.

sentences.zh: 八音清少變徵，得全度五十三分之半。

translations.literal: Eighth degree clear lesser altered zhi obtains half of the full degree of fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: The eighth degree, clear lesser altered fourth, yields half the full length of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 為二十六，小餘六三。

translations.literal: Making twenty-six, remainder sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: That is twenty-six, with a remainder of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 弦音旋宮轉調，其要有四：一，定弦音應某律呂聲字，即得某弦度分。

translations.literal: String tones circling gong and shifting mode—the essentials are four. First: when the fixed string tone corresponds to a certain pitch-pipe note character, one obtains that string's degree-parts.
translations.idiomatic: In the circulation of modes and shifting of keys on string instruments, four essentials apply. First: when a tuned string pitch matches the note character of a given pitch standard, one obtains the degree-parts for that string.

sentences.zh: 如倍無射之律變宮合字定弦，則得徵弦之分；

translations.literal: For example, fixing strings to the "he" character of the doubled Wushe pitch-pipe's altered gong yields the zhi-string's degree-parts.
translations.idiomatic: For example, tuning to the "he" note of the doubled Wushe pipe's altered leading tone yields the fifth-string degree-parts.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾之律宮聲四字定弦，則得羽弦之分；

translations.literal: Fixing strings to the "si" character of the Huangzhong pitch-pipe's gong tone yields the yu-string's degree-parts.
translations.idiomatic: Tuning to the "si" note of Huangzhong's tonic yields the sixth-string degree-parts.

sentences.zh: 太簇之律商聲乙字定弦，則得變宮弦之分；

translations.literal: Fixing strings to the "yi" character of the Taicu pitch-pipe's shang tone yields the altered-gong-string's degree-parts.
translations.idiomatic: Tuning to the "yi" note of Taicu's second yields the altered-leading-tone string's degree-parts.

sentences.zh: 姑洗之律角聲上字定弦，則得宮弦之分；

translations.literal: Fixing strings to the "shang" character of the Guxian pitch-pipe's jue tone yields the gong-string's degree-parts.
translations.idiomatic: Tuning to the "shang" note of Guxian's third yields the tonic string's degree-parts.

sentences.zh: 蕤賓之律變徵尺字定弦，則得商弦之分；

translations.literal: Fixing strings to the "chi" character of the Ruibin pitch-pipe's altered zhi yields the shang-string's degree-parts.
translations.idiomatic: Tuning to the "chi" note of Ruibin's altered fourth yields the second-string degree-parts.

sentences.zh: 夷則之律徵聲宮字定弦，則得羽弦之分；

translations.literal: Fixing strings to the "gong" character of the Yize pitch-pipe's zhi tone yields the yu-string's degree-parts;
translations.idiomatic: Tuning to the "gong" note of Yize's fifth yields the sixth-string degree-parts;

sentences.zh: 無射之律羽聲凡字定弦，則得變徵弦之分。

translations.literal: Fixing strings to the "fan" character of the Wushe pitch-pipe's yu tone yields the altered-zhi-string's degree-parts.
translations.idiomatic: Tuning to the "fan" note of Wushe's sixth yields the altered-fourth string's degree-parts.

sentences.zh: 此陽律一均七聲定弦之正分也。

translations.literal: These are the proper degree-parts for fixing strings to the seven tones within one yang-pipe octave.
translations.idiomatic: These are the standard degree-parts for tuning all seven tones across one yang-pipe octave.

sentences.zh: 陰呂定弦七聲之分亦如之。

translations.literal: The degree-parts for fixing strings to the seven yin-pipe tones follow likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The same principle applies to degree-parts for tuning the seven yin-pipe tones.

sentences.zh: 一，弦音轉調不能依次遞遷，必以宮調為準，故七聲因之而變。

translations.literal: First: string-tone mode-shifting cannot proceed by sequential degrees; it must take the gong mode as standard, and therefore the seven tones change accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: First: transposing string tones cannot simply proceed step by step through the scale; the tonic mode must serve as the reference, and the seven tones shift accordingly.

sentences.zh: 如琴之正調為宮調，其商調以七弦遞高一音，但六弦、七弦太急易，或變宮調以七弦遞下一音，則一弦、二弦又慢不成聲，故宮調七弦立准，轉調則七弦內有更者，有不更者，有宜緊者，有宜慢者，弦之轉移間，宮調旋焉。

translations.literal: For example, when the qin's standard tuning is the gong mode, its shang mode raises each of the seven strings by one tone, but the sixth and seventh strings become too taut and snap; or if one shifts to altered-gong mode by lowering the seventh string one tone, then the first and second strings slacken and fail to sound. Therefore the gong mode's seven strings establish the standard; in shifting modes, among the seven strings some change, some do not, some should be tightened, some loosened—and in the transfer among strings, the gong mode cycles accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Take the qin: in standard tonic tuning, the second-mode transposition raises every string a whole step—but the sixth and seventh strings grow painfully tight and break. Lowering only the seventh string to reach altered-leading-tone mode leaves the first and second too slack to sound. The seven strings of tonic mode must therefore anchor all transpositions: some strings change, some stay fixed, some must be tightened, others loosened—and as strings are retuned, the tonic frame itself rotates.

sentences.zh: 如一弦、三弦、六弦俱慢下管律一音，在弦度為半分，而餘弦不移，即轉為商調。

translations.literal: For example, if the first, third, and sixth strings all slacken down one pitch-pipe tone—in string degree, half a part—while the remaining strings do not move, this shifts to shang mode.
translations.idiomatic: For instance, if the first, third, and sixth strings are each loosened one pitch-pipe degree—half a string-part—while the rest stay put, the instrument becomes shang mode.

sentences.zh: 蓋正宮調一弦、六弦定倍無射之律；

translations.literal: For the standard gong mode, the first and sixth strings are fixed to the doubled Wushe pitch-pipe;
translations.idiomatic: In standard tonic mode, the first and sixth strings are tuned to the doubled Wushe pipe;

sentences.zh: 變宮合字得徵弦分者，下為倍夷則之律；

translations.literal: where the "he" character of altered gong yields zhi-string degree-parts, lowering yields the doubled Yize pitch-pipe;
translations.idiomatic: and where altered-gong's "he" note gives fifth-string degree-parts, lowering produces the doubled Yize pipe;

sentences.zh: 羽聲凡字轉角弦之分，三弦定姑洗之律；

translations.literal: the "fan" character of yu tone shifting to jue-string degree-parts—the third string fixed to the Guxian pitch-pipe;
translations.idiomatic: the "fan" note of the sixth, now yielding third-string degree-parts—the third string set to Guxian;

sentences.zh: 角聲上字得宮弦分者，下為太簇之律，商聲乙字轉羽弦之分，其二弦、四弦、五弦、七弦不移者，仍應本律。

translations.literal: the "shang" character of jue tone yielding gong-string degree-parts, lowering to the Taicu pitch-pipe; the "yi" character of shang tone shifting to yu-string degree-parts; the second, fourth, fifth, and seventh strings, not moved, still correspond to their original pitch-pipes.
translations.idiomatic: the "shang" note of the third, yielding tonic-string parts, lowered to Taicu; the "yi" note of the second, now yielding sixth-string parts. The second, fourth, fifth, and seventh strings, left unchanged, still sound their original pipes.

sentences.zh: 但二弦、七弦原得羽弦分者，轉為徵弦之分；

translations.literal: But the second and seventh strings, which originally had yu-string degree-parts, shift to zhi-string degree-parts;
translations.idiomatic: But the second and seventh strings, originally at sixth-string pitch, now take fifth-string degree-parts;

sentences.zh: 四弦原得商弦分者，轉為宮弦之分；

translations.literal: the fourth string, which originally had shang-string degree-parts, shifts to gong-string degree-parts;
translations.idiomatic: the fourth, originally at second-string pitch, becomes tonic-string pitch;

sentences.zh: 五弦原得角弦分者，轉為商弦之分。

translations.literal: the fifth string, which originally had jue-string degree-parts, shifts to shang-string degree-parts.
translations.idiomatic: and the fifth, originally at third-string pitch, becomes second-string pitch.

sentences.zh: 其倍無射之律，變宮合字為徵弦分者，轉變徵應於倍應鍾之呂，清變宮高六，應姑洗之律；

translations.literal: Of the doubled Wushe pitch-pipe, where altered-gong's "he" character serves as zhi-string degree-parts, the altered zhi shifts to correspond to the doubled Yingzhong yin-pipe; raised altered gong "liu" corresponds to the Guxian pitch-pipe;
translations.idiomatic: On the doubled Wushe standard, where altered-gong's "he" serves as fifth-string pitch, altered-fourth moves to doubled Yingzhong; raised altered-gong "liu" answers to Guxian;

sentences.zh: 角聲上字為宮弦分者，轉變宮應於仲呂之呂，清角高上，此二分當二變不用。

translations.literal: where jue tone's "shang" character serves as gong-string degree-parts, altered gong shifts to correspond to the Zhonglü yin-pipe; raised jue "shang"—these two degree-parts correspond to the two altered tones and are not used.
translations.idiomatic: where the third's "shang" note serves as tonic-string pitch, altered-leading-tone shifts to Zhonglü; raised third "shang"—these two degree-parts map to the altered tones and are set aside.

sentences.zh: 因三弦定太簇之律，商聲乙字得羽弦之分以起調，四弦原得商弦之分者，轉為宮弦之分以立宮，故曰商調。

translations.literal: Because the third string is fixed to the Taicu pitch-pipe, the "yi" character of shang tone yields yu-string degree-parts to establish the mode; the fourth string, which originally had shang-string degree-parts, shifts to gong-string degree-parts to establish the tonic—hence it is called shang mode.
translations.idiomatic: Since the third string is set to Taicu, the second's "yi" note, yielding sixth-string pitch, opens the mode; the fourth, formerly at second-string pitch, becomes tonic-string pitch to establish the tonic—hence shang mode.

sentences.zh: 如二弦、四弦、五弦、七弦俱緊上管律半音，在弦度亦為半分，而餘弦不移，即轉為角調。

translations.literal: For example, if the second, fourth, fifth, and seventh strings all tighten up half a pitch-pipe tone—in string degree also half a part—while the remaining strings do not move, this shifts to jue mode.
translations.idiomatic: If the second, fourth, fifth, and seventh strings are each tightened a half pitch-pipe degree—half a string-part—while the others stay put, the instrument becomes jue mode.

sentences.zh: 蓋正宮調二弦、七弦定黃鍾之律，宮聲四字得羽弦分者，上為大呂之呂，清宮高五轉徵弦之分。

translations.literal: For the standard gong mode, the second and seventh strings are fixed to the Huangzhong pitch-pipe; where gong tone's "si" character yields yu-string degree-parts, raising to the Dalü yin-pipe, raised gong "wu" shifts to zhi-string degree-parts.
translations.idiomatic: In standard tonic mode, the second and seventh strings are tuned to Huangzhong; where the tonic's "si" note gives sixth-string pitch, raising to Dalü and the raised tonic "wu" yields fifth-string degree-parts.

sentences.zh: 四弦定蕤賓之律，變徵尺字得商弦分者，上為林鍾之呂，清變徵高尺轉宮弦之分。

translations.literal: The fourth string is fixed to the Ruibin pitch-pipe; where altered zhi's "chi" character yields shang-string degree-parts, raising to the Linzhong yin-pipe, raised altered zhi "chi" shifts to gong-string degree-parts.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth string is set to Ruibin; where altered-fourth's "chi" note gives second-string pitch, raising to Linzhong and the raised altered-fourth "chi" yields tonic-string degree-parts.

sentences.zh: 五弦定夷則之律，徵聲工字得角弦分者，上為南呂之呂，清徵高工轉商弦之分。

translations.literal: The fifth string is fixed to the Yize pitch-pipe; where zhi tone's "gong" character yields jue-string degree-parts, raising to the Nanlü yin-pipe, raised zhi "gong" shifts to shang-string degree-parts.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth string is set to Yize; where the fifth's "gong" note gives third-string pitch, raising to Nanlü and the raised fifth "gong" yields second-string degree-parts.

sentences.zh: 其一弦、三弦、六弦不移，仍應本律，但一弦、六弦轉為角分，三弦轉為羽分，而轉變徵、變宮者不用。

translations.literal: The first, third, and sixth strings do not move and still correspond to their original pitch-pipes, but the first and sixth shift to jue degree-parts, the third to yu degree-parts, while the shifted altered zhi and altered gong are not used.
translations.idiomatic: The first, third, and sixth strings stay put and still sound their original pipes, but the first and sixth now yield third-string parts, the third yields sixth-string parts, while the shifted altered-fourth and altered-leading-tone are set aside.

sentences.zh: 因三弦應姑洗之律，角聲上字得羽弦之分以起調，四弦原得商弦之分者，上為角弦之分，轉宮弦之分以立宮，故曰角調。

translations.literal: Because the third string corresponds to the Guxian pitch-pipe, jue tone's "shang" character yields yu-string degree-parts to establish the mode; the fourth string, which originally had shang-string degree-parts, raises to jue-string degree-parts and shifts to gong-string degree-parts to establish the tonic—hence it is called jue mode.
translations.idiomatic: Since the third string answers to Guxian, the third's "shang" note, yielding sixth-string pitch, opens the mode; the fourth, formerly at second-string pitch, rises to third-string pitch and becomes tonic-string pitch to establish the tonic—hence jue mode.

sentences.zh: 如獨緊五弦管律半音，在弦度亦為半分，即轉為變徵調。

translations.literal: For example, if only the fifth string is tightened half a pitch-pipe tone—in string degree also half a part—this shifts to altered-zhi mode.
translations.idiomatic: If only the fifth string is tightened a half pitch-pipe degree—half a string-part—the instrument becomes altered-fourth mode.

sentences.zh: 四弦應蕤賓之律，變徵尺字得羽弦之分以起調。

translations.literal: The fourth string corresponds to the Ruibin pitch-pipe; altered zhi's "chi" character yields yu-string degree-parts to establish the mode.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth string answers to Ruibin; altered-fourth's "chi" note, yielding sixth-string pitch, opens the mode.

sentences.zh: 五弦原得角弦之分者，上為變徵之分，轉為宮弦之分以立宮，故曰變徵調。

translations.literal: The fifth string, which originally had jue-string degree-parts, raises to altered-zhi degree-parts and shifts to gong-string degree-parts to establish the tonic—hence it is called altered-zhi mode.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth, originally at third-string pitch, rises to altered-fourth pitch and becomes tonic-string pitch to establish the tonic—hence altered-fourth mode.

sentences.zh: 如獨慢三弦管律一音，在弦度為半分，即轉為徵調，因五弦應夷則之律，徵聲工字得羽弦之分以起調，一弦、六弦原得徵弦之分者，轉為宮弦之分以立宮，故曰徵調。

translations.literal: For example, if only the third string slackens one pitch-pipe tone—in string degree, half a part—this shifts to zhi mode; because the fifth string corresponds to the Yize pitch-pipe, zhi tone's "gong" character yields yu-string degree-parts to establish the mode; the first and sixth strings, which originally had zhi-string degree-parts, shift to gong-string degree-parts to establish the tonic—hence it is called zhi mode.
translations.idiomatic: If only the third string is loosened one pitch-pipe degree—half a string-part—the instrument becomes fifth mode; since the fifth string answers to Yize, the fifth's "gong" note, yielding sixth-string pitch, opens the mode; the first and sixth, originally at fifth-string pitch, become tonic-string pitch to establish the tonic—hence fifth mode.

sentences.zh: 如以一弦、三弦、六弦慢下管律一音，四弦慢下管律半音，在弦度俱為半分，即轉為羽調，因一弦、六弦應倍夷則之律，羽聲凡字得羽弦之分以起調，二弦、七弦原得羽弦分者，上為變宮之分，轉宮弦之分以立宮，故曰變宮調也。

translations.literal: For example, if the first, third, and sixth strings slacken one pitch-pipe tone and the fourth slackens half a pitch-pipe tone—in string degree all half a part—this shifts to yu mode; because the first and sixth strings correspond to the doubled Yize pitch-pipe, yu tone's "fan" character yields yu-string degree-parts to establish the mode; the second and seventh strings, which originally had yu-string degree-parts, raise to altered-gong degree-parts and shift to gong-string degree-parts to establish the tonic—hence it is called altered-gong mode.
translations.idiomatic: If the first, third, and sixth strings are loosened one pitch-pipe degree and the fourth a half degree—all half string-parts—the instrument becomes sixth mode; since the first and sixth answer to doubled Yize, the sixth's "fan" note, yielding sixth-string pitch, opens the mode; the second and seventh, originally at sixth-string pitch, rise to altered-leading-tone pitch and become tonic-string pitch to establish the tonic—hence altered-leading-tone mode.

sentences.zh: 一，弦音諸調雖無二變，而定弦取音，必審二變之聲，必計二變之分。

translations.literal: First: although the various string-tone modes may lack the two altered tones, in fixing strings and taking pitches one must examine the sounds of the two altered tones and must calculate their degree-parts.
translations.idiomatic: First: even when a string mode omits the two altered tones in performance, tuning and pitch-taking must still account for those altered tones and their degree-parts.

sentences.zh: 如陽律一均，即徵弦七聲之分言之，散聲為全分首音，其二音與羽弦應者為羽分，三音與變宮弦應者為變宮分，至七音與變徵弦應者為變徵分，八音仍與全弦應，故為旋於首音。

translations.literal: For example, within one yang-pipe octave—speaking of the zhi-string's seven-tone degree-parts—the open string is the whole-part first tone; the second tone, corresponding to the yu string, is the yu part; the third, corresponding to the altered-gong string, is the altered-gong part; up to the seventh, corresponding to the altered-zhi string, which is the altered-zhi part; the eighth tone again corresponds to the full string—thus it cycles back to the first tone.
translations.idiomatic: Within one yang-pipe octave, consider the fifth-string's seven-tone degree-parts: the open string is the whole-part root; the second tone, matching the sixth string, is the sixth part; the third, matching the altered-leading-tone string, is the altered-leading-tone part; the seventh, matching the altered-fourth string, is the altered-fourth part; the eighth returns to the full string—completing the cycle at the root.

sentences.zh: 其各分與各弦相應，亦自與各律相應。

translations.literal: Each degree-part corresponds to its string and likewise to its pitch-pipe.
translations.idiomatic: Each degree-part aligns with its string and, in turn, with its pitch standard.

sentences.zh: 計其分，則首音徵至二音羽，三音羽至三音變宮，皆得全分。

translations.literal: Calculating the parts: from the first tone zhi to the second tone yu, and from the third tone yu to the third tone altered gong, all yield whole parts.
translations.idiomatic: Measured in parts: from the root fifth to the second sixth, and from the third sixth to the third altered leading tone, each span equals a whole part.

sentences.zh: 三音變宮至四音宮，祗得半分。

translations.literal: From the third tone altered gong to the fourth tone gong, only half a part is obtained.
translations.idiomatic: From the third altered leading tone to the fourth tonic, only half a part is obtained.

sentences.zh: 四音宮至五音商，五音商至六音角，六音角至七音變徵，皆得全分。

translations.literal: From the fourth tone gong to the fifth tone shang, from the fifth shang to the sixth jue, and from the sixth jue to the seventh altered zhi, all yield whole parts.
translations.idiomatic: From the fourth tonic to the fifth second, from the fifth second to the sixth third, and from the sixth third to the seventh altered fourth, each span equals a whole part.

sentences.zh: 七音變徵至八音徵，亦得半分。

translations.literal: From the seventh tone altered zhi to the eighth tone zhi, also half a part is obtained.
translations.idiomatic: From the seventh altered fourth to the eighth fifth, likewise only half a part is obtained.

sentences.zh: 以宮弦七聲之分言之，散聲為全半首音，其二音與商弦應者為商分，與角弦應者為角分，三至七音與變宮弦應者為變宮分，八音仍與全弦應。

translations.literal: Speaking of the gong-string's seven-tone degree-parts, the open string is the whole-and-half first tone; the second tone, corresponding to the shang string, is the shang part; corresponding to the jue string, the jue part; tones three through seven, corresponding to the altered-gong string, are the altered-gong part; the eighth tone again corresponds to the full string.
translations.idiomatic: On the tonic string's seven-tone degree-parts, the open string is the whole-and-half root; the second tone, matching the second string, is the second part; matching the third string, the third part; tones three through seven, matching the altered-leading-tone string, are the altered-leading-tone part; the eighth returns to the full string.

sentences.zh: 而四音變徵至五音徵，七音變宮至八音宮，皆祗半分。

translations.literal: But from the fourth tone altered zhi to the fifth tone zhi, and from the seventh tone altered gong to the eighth tone gong, all are only half parts.
translations.idiomatic: But from the fourth altered fourth to the fifth fifth, and from the seventh altered leading tone to the eighth tonic, each span is only half a part.

sentences.zh: 蓋太簇商聲乙字所應之弦分至姑洗角聲上字所應之弦分，與無射羽聲凡字所應之弦分至半黃鍾變宮合字所應之弦分，其間必為半分，故各弦七聲之分不移，而所應聲律有間雜之別。

translations.literal: For the string degree-parts corresponding to Taicu shang tone's "yi" character through to Guxian jue tone's "shang" character, and from Wushe yu tone's "fan" character through to half-Huangzhong altered gong's "he" character, the intervals between must be half parts; therefore each string's seven-tone degree-parts do not shift, yet the pitch-pipes they correspond to have distinctions of mixed intervals.
translations.idiomatic: Between the string parts for Taicu's "yi" and Guxian's "shang", and between those for Wushe's "fan" and half-Huangzhong altered-gong's "he", the intervals must be half parts; thus each string's seven-tone layout stays fixed, while the pitch standards they answer to vary in their mixed whole- and half-step spacing.

sentences.zh: 各分全半之間，宮調旋焉。

translations.literal: Between whole and half parts, the gong mode cycles accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: In the alternation of whole and half parts, the tonic mode rotates into place.

sentences.zh: 以宮調七弦為準，據每調徵弦七聲言之，商調之徵，乃宮調之羽轉而為徵分者也。

translations.literal: Taking the gong mode's seven strings as standard, speaking of each mode's zhi-string seven tones: the zhi of shang mode is the yu of gong mode shifted to become zhi degree-parts.
translations.idiomatic: With tonic mode's seven strings as the reference, consider each mode's fifth-string seven tones: in shang mode, the fifth is tonic mode's sixth retuned to fifth-string degree-parts.

sentences.zh: 宮弦之羽，全弦首音為羽，其變宮變徵在二音、六音，是二音至三音，六音至七音，為半分也。

translations.literal: On the gong string's yu, the full-string first tone is yu; its altered gong and altered zhi fall on the second and sixth tones—thus from the second to the third tone, and from the sixth to the seventh, are half parts.
translations.idiomatic: On the tonic string as sixth, the open string is the sixth; altered leading tone and altered fourth fall on the second and sixth degrees—so the second-to-third and sixth-to-seventh spans are half parts.

sentences.zh: 今全弦轉為徵，則變宮、變徵在三音、七音，是三音至四音，七音至八音，為半分矣。

translations.literal: Now when the full string shifts to zhi, altered gong and altered zhi fall on the third and seventh tones—thus from the third to the fourth tone, and from the seventh to the eighth, are half parts.
translations.idiomatic: When that string is retuned as fifth, altered leading tone and altered fourth move to the third and seventh degrees—so the third-to-fourth and seventh-to-eighth spans become half parts.

sentences.zh: 故全弦定黃鍾之律宮聲四字者不移，二音即應太簇之律商聲乙字，其間得全分三音。

translations.literal: Therefore the full string fixed to Huangzhong pitch-pipe gong tone's "si" character does not shift; the second tone immediately corresponds to Taicu pitch-pipe shang tone's "yi" character, and the interval to the third tone yields a whole part.
translations.idiomatic: The open string, still tuned to Huangzhong tonic "si", stays put; the second degree answers to Taicu second "yi", and the span to the third yields a whole part.

sentences.zh: 若取姑洗之律角聲上字，則二音至三音為半分，仍與宮調之羽同，是以必取仲呂之呂清角高上，其間弦度始得全分，其四音仍應蕤賓之律變徵尺字。

translations.literal: If one takes Guxian pitch-pipe jue tone's "shang" character, then from the second to the third tone is a half part—the same as gong mode's yu; therefore one must take Zhonglü yin-pipe's raised jue "shang", and only then does the string degree between yield a whole part; the fourth tone still corresponds to Ruibin pitch-pipe altered zhi's "chi" character.
translations.idiomatic: If one used Guxian third "shang", the second-to-third span would be a half part—as in tonic mode's sixth—so one must take Zhonglü's raised third "shang" to obtain a whole string-part; the fourth degree still answers to Ruibin altered-fourth "chi".

sentences.zh: 蓋太簇乙字至姑洗上字為半分，加仲呂高上之半分，得一全分，而仲呂高上至蕤賓尺字為半分，此所以二音至三音得全分，為羽至變宮，而三音至四音為半分，乃變宮至宮分也。

translations.literal: For from Taicu "yi" to Guxian "shang" is a half part; adding Zhonglü raised "shang"'s half part yields one whole part; and from Zhonglü raised "shang" to Ruibin "chi" is a half part—this is why from the second to the third tone a whole part is obtained, as yu to altered gong, while from the third to the fourth is a half part, being altered gong to gong.
translations.idiomatic: From Taicu "yi" to Guxian "shang" is a half part; add Zhonglü raised "shang"'s half part and one whole part results; from Zhonglü raised "shang" to Ruibin "chi" is another half part—hence the second-to-third span is a whole part (sixth to altered leading tone), while the third-to-fourth is a half part (altered leading tone to tonic).

sentences.zh: 五音仍應夷則之律徵聲工字，六音仍應無射之律羽聲凡字，此四音至五音，五音至六音，亦得全分。

translations.literal: The fifth tone still corresponds to Yize pitch-pipe zhi tone's "gong" character, the sixth to Wushe pitch-pipe yu tone's "fan" character—from the fourth to the fifth tone and from the fifth to the sixth, whole parts are also obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth degree still answers to Yize fifth "gong", the sixth to Wushe sixth "fan"—the fourth-to-fifth and fifth-to-sixth spans likewise yield whole parts.

sentences.zh: 至七音若取半黃鍾之律變宮合字，則六音至七音為半分，亦與宮調之羽同，必取半大呂之呂清變宮高六，其間弦度始得全分，其八音仍與首音同應黃鍾之律宮聲四字。

translations.literal: For the seventh tone, if one takes half-Huangzhong pitch-pipe altered gong's "he" character, then from the sixth to the seventh tone is a half part—the same as gong mode's yu; one must take half-Dalü yin-pipe's raised altered gong "liu", and only then does the string degree between yield a whole part; the eighth tone still corresponds with the first to Huangzhong pitch-pipe gong tone's "si" character.
translations.idiomatic: For the seventh degree, if one used half-Huangzhong altered-gong "he", the sixth-to-seventh span would be a half part—as in tonic mode's sixth—so one must take half-Dalü's raised altered-gong "liu" to obtain a whole string-part; the eighth returns with the root to Huangzhong tonic "si".

sentences.zh: 蓋無射凡字至半黃鍾合字為半分，加半大呂高六之半分，得一全分，而半大呂高六至黃鍾四字為半分，此所以六音至七音得全分，為角至變徵，而七音至八音為半分，乃變徵至徵分也。

translations.literal: For from Wushe "fan" to half-Huangzhong "he" is a half part; adding half-Dalü raised "liu"'s half part yields one whole part; and from half-Dalü raised "liu" to Huangzhong "si" is a half part—this is why from the sixth to the seventh tone a whole part is obtained, as jue to altered zhi, while from the seventh to the eighth is a half part, being altered zhi to zhi.
translations.idiomatic: From Wushe "fan" to half-Huangzhong "he" is a half part; add half-Dalü raised "liu"'s half part and one whole part results; from half-Dalü raised "liu" to Huangzhong "si" is another half part—hence the sixth-to-seventh span is a whole part (third to altered fourth), while the seventh-to-eighth is a half part (altered fourth to fifth).

sentences.zh: 角調之徵，乃宮調之變宮與清宮調之羽相雜而為徵分者也。

translations.literal: The zhi of jue mode is gong mode's altered gong mixed with raised-gong mode's yu to become zhi degree-parts.
translations.idiomatic: In jue mode, the fifth combines tonic mode's altered leading tone with raised-tonic mode's sixth to form fifth-string degree-parts.

sentences.zh: 宮調之變宮全弦首音即變宮，而變徵在五音，是首音至二音，五音至六音，為半分也。

translations.literal: Gong mode's altered gong on the full string has the first tone as altered gong, while altered zhi falls on the fifth tone—thus from the first to the second tone, and from the fifth to the sixth, are half parts.
translations.idiomatic: In tonic mode's altered-leading-tone string, the open string is altered leading tone and altered fourth falls on the fifth degree—so the first-to-second and fifth-to-sixth spans are half parts.

sentences.zh: 清商調之羽全弦首音為清羽，其清變宮、清變徵在二音、六音，是又二音至三音，六音至七音，為半分也，今全弦轉為徵，則三音至四音，七音至八音，為半分矣。

translations.literal: Raised-shang mode's yu on the full string has the first tone as raised yu; its raised altered gong and raised altered zhi fall on the second and sixth tones—thus again from the second to the third tone, and from the sixth to the seventh, are half parts; now when the full string shifts to zhi, from the third to the fourth tone, and from the seventh to the eighth, are half parts.
translations.idiomatic: On raised-second mode's sixth string, the open note is raised sixth; raised altered leading tone and raised altered fourth fall on the second and sixth degrees—again making the second-to-third and sixth-to-seventh spans half parts; retuned as fifth, the third-to-fourth and seventh-to-eighth spans become half parts.

sentences.zh: 首音若仍定太簇之律商聲乙字，則首音徵至二音羽所得全分，必當取於仲呂之呂清角高上，其本調羽弦，則亦應仲呂之呂清角高上，是清角調非正角調矣。

translations.literal: If the first tone remains fixed to Taicu pitch-pipe shang tone's "yi" character, then the whole part obtained from the first tone zhi to the second tone yu must be taken from Zhonglü yin-pipe's raised jue "shang"; its home-mode yu string would also correspond to Zhonglü yin-pipe's raised jue "shang"—this would be raised-jue mode, not standard jue mode.
translations.idiomatic: If the root stayed at Taicu second "yi", the whole part from fifth to sixth would have to come from Zhonglü's raised third "shang"—and the home-mode sixth string would answer to that same note—making it raised-third mode, not standard third mode.

sentences.zh: 因取姑洗之律角聲上字為正角調，故起調於羽弦者，必取姑洗正角聲，而徵弦羽分亦當應姑洗之律。

translations.literal: Because Guxian pitch-pipe jue tone's "shang" character is taken for standard jue mode, therefore in establishing the mode on the yu string one must take Guxian's standard jue tone, and the zhi string's yu part must also correspond to the Guxian pitch-pipe.
translations.idiomatic: Since Guxian third "shang" defines standard third mode, opening the mode on the sixth string requires Guxian's standard third—and the fifth string's sixth part must answer to Guxian as well.

sentences.zh: 是以角調徵弦散聲首音，反比正宮調變宮弦之散聲首音下半音，取清宮調之羽弦散聲，大呂之呂清宮高五，其分始合，蓋因本調羽聲得正角之律故也。

translations.literal: Therefore the open-string first tone of jue mode's zhi string is, conversely, a half tone below the open-string first tone of standard gong mode's altered-gong string; one takes raised-gong mode's yu string open string—Dalü yin-pipe's raised gong "wu"—and only then do the degree-parts align, because the home-mode yu tone obtains the standard jue pitch-pipe.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the open root of jue mode's fifth string sits a semitone below standard tonic mode's altered-leading-tone open string; one takes raised-tonic mode's sixth-string open note—Dalü raised tonic "wu"—and only then do the parts align, since the home-mode sixth must sound the standard third pipe.

sentences.zh: 二音應姑洗之律角聲上字為羽分，三音應蕤賓之律變徵尺字為變宮分，四音應林鍾之呂清變徵高尺為宮分，五音應南呂之呂清徵高工為商分，六音應半黃鍾之律正變宮六字為角分，七音應黃鍾之律正宮四字為變徵分，八音仍應大呂之呂清宮高五，是則三音蕤賓至四音林鍾為半分，七音黃鍾至八音大呂為半分，正為本調徵弦之變宮至宮，變徵至徵之二半分也。

translations.literal: The second tone corresponds to Guxian pitch-pipe jue tone's "shang" character as the yu part; the third to Ruibin pitch-pipe altered zhi's "chi" as the altered-gong part; the fourth to Linzhong yin-pipe's raised altered zhi "chi" as the gong part; the fifth to Nanlü yin-pipe's raised zhi "gong" as the shang part; the sixth to half-Huangzhong pitch-pipe's standard altered gong "liu" as the jue part; the seventh to Huangzhong pitch-pipe's standard gong "si" as the altered-zhi part; the eighth still corresponds to Dalü yin-pipe's raised gong "wu"—thus from the third tone Ruibin to the fourth Linzhong is a half part, and from the seventh Huangzhong to the eighth Dalü is a half part, precisely the two half parts of this mode's zhi string from altered gong to gong and from altered zhi to zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The second answers to Guxian third "shang" as the sixth part; the third to Ruibin altered-fourth "chi" as altered-leading-tone part; the fourth to Linzhong raised altered-fourth "chi" as tonic part; the fifth to Nanlü raised fifth "gong" as second part; the sixth to half-Huangzhong standard altered-gong "liu" as third part; the seventh to Huangzhong standard tonic "si" as altered-fourth part; the eighth returns to Dalü raised tonic "wu"—Ruibin-to-Linzhong and Huangzhong-to-Dalü are half parts, exactly this mode's fifth-string half steps from altered leading tone to tonic and from altered fourth to fifth.

sentences.zh: 變徵調之徵，乃宮調之宮轉而徵分者也。

translations.literal: The zhi of altered-zhi mode is gong mode's gong shifted to become zhi degree-parts.
translations.idiomatic: In altered-fourth mode, the fifth is tonic mode's tonic retuned to fifth-string degree-parts.

sentences.zh: 宮調之宮，變徵、變宮在四音、七音，是四音至五音，七音至八音，為半分也。

translations.literal: Gong mode's gong has altered zhi and altered gong on the fourth and seventh tones—thus from the fourth to the fifth tone, and from the seventh to the eighth, are half parts.
translations.idiomatic: In tonic mode's tonic string, altered fourth and altered leading tone fall on the fourth and seventh degrees—so the fourth-to-fifth and seventh-to-eighth spans are half parts.

sentences.zh: 今全弦轉為徵，則三音至四音，七音至八音，為半分，移宮調之宮四音至五音半分，為三音至四音半分，則四音取南呂之呂清徵高工，三音夷則至四音南呂為半分，七音太簇至八音姑洗為半分。

translations.literal: Now when the full string shifts to zhi, from the third to the fourth tone, and from the seventh to the eighth, are half parts; shifting gong mode's gong fourth-to-fifth half part to third-to-fourth half part, the fourth tone takes Nanlü yin-pipe's raised zhi "gong"; from the third tone Yize to the fourth Nanlü is a half part, and from the seventh Taicu to the eighth Guxian is a half part.
translations.idiomatic: Retuned as fifth, the third-to-fourth and seventh-to-eighth spans become half parts; tonic mode's tonic fourth-to-fifth half step moves to third-to-fourth—the fourth takes Nanlü raised fifth "gong"; Yize-to-Nanlü and Taicu-to-Guxian are each half parts.

sentences.zh: 徵調之徵，乃宮調之商轉而為徵者也。

translations.literal: The zhi of zhi mode is gong mode's shang shifted to become zhi.
translations.idiomatic: In fifth mode, the fifth is tonic mode's second retuned to fifth-string pitch.

sentences.zh: 宮調之商，變徵、變宮在三音、六音，是三音至四音，六音至七音，為半分也。

translations.literal: Gong mode's shang has altered zhi and altered gong on the third and sixth tones—thus from the third to the fourth tone, and from the sixth to the seventh, are half parts.
translations.idiomatic: In tonic mode's second string, altered fourth and altered leading tone fall on the third and sixth degrees—so the third-to-fourth and sixth-to-seventh spans are half parts.

sentences.zh: 今全弦轉為徵，則三音至四音，七音至八音，為半分，移宮調之商六音至七音半分，為七音至八音半分，則七音取仲呂之呂清角高上，三音無射至四音半黃鍾為半分，七音仲呂至八音蕤賓為半分。

translations.literal: Now when the full string shifts to zhi, from the third to the fourth tone, and from the seventh to the eighth, are half parts; shifting gong mode's shang sixth-to-seventh half part to seventh-to-eighth half part, the seventh tone takes Zhonglü yin-pipe's raised jue "shang"; from the third tone Wushe to the fourth half-Huangzhong is a half part, and from the seventh Zhonglü to the eighth Ruibin is a half part.
translations.idiomatic: Retuned as fifth, the third-to-fourth and seventh-to-eighth spans become half parts; tonic mode's second sixth-to-seventh half step moves to seventh-to-eighth—the seventh takes Zhonglü raised third "shang"; Wushe-to-half-Huangzhong and Zhonglü-to-Ruibin are each half parts.

sentences.zh: 羽調之徵，乃宮調之角轉而為徵分者也。

translations.literal: The zhi of yu mode is gong mode's jue shifted to become zhi degree-parts.
translations.idiomatic: In sixth mode, the fifth is tonic mode's third retuned to fifth-string degree-parts.

sentences.zh: 宮調之角，變徵、變宮在六音、五音，是二音至三音，五音至六音，為半分也。

translations.literal: Gong mode's jue has altered zhi and altered gong on the sixth and fifth tones—thus from the second to the third tone, and from the fifth to the sixth, are half parts.
translations.idiomatic: In tonic mode's third string, altered fourth and altered leading tone fall on the sixth and fifth degrees—so the second-to-third and fifth-to-sixth spans are half parts.

sentences.zh: 今全弦轉為徵，則三音至四音，七音至八音，為半分也。

translations.literal: Now when the full string shifts to zhi, from the third to the fourth tone, and from the seventh to the eighth, are half parts.
translations.idiomatic: Retuned as fifth, the third-to-fourth and seventh-to-eighth spans become half parts.

sentences.zh: 移宮調之商二音至三音半分、五音至六音半分，為三音至四音半分、七音至八音半分，則三音取半大呂之呂清變宮高五，六音取仲呂之呂清角高上，七音取林鍾之呂清變徵高尺，三音半大呂至四音黃鍾為半分，七音林鍾至八音夷則為半分。

translations.literal: Shifting gong mode's shang second-to-third and fifth-to-sixth half parts to third-to-fourth and seventh-to-eighth half parts, the third tone takes half-Dalü yin-pipe's raised altered gong "wu", the sixth takes Zhonglü yin-pipe's raised jue "shang", the seventh takes Linzhong yin-pipe's raised altered zhi "chi"; from the third tone half-Dalü to the fourth Huangzhong is a half part, and from the seventh Linzhong to the eighth Yize is a half part.
translations.idiomatic: Tonic mode's second-string second-to-third and fifth-to-sixth half steps move to third-to-fourth and seventh-to-eighth—the third takes half-Dalü raised altered-gong "wu", the sixth Zhonglü raised third "shang", the seventh Linzhong raised altered-fourth "chi"; half-Dalü-to-Huangzhong and Linzhong-to-Yize are each half parts.

sentences.zh: 變宮調之徵，乃宮調之變徵與清宮調之角相雜而為徵分者也。

translations.literal: The zhi of altered-gong mode is gong mode's altered zhi mixed with raised-gong mode's jue to become zhi degree-parts.
translations.idiomatic: In altered-leading-tone mode, the fifth combines tonic mode's altered fourth with raised-tonic mode's third to form fifth-string degree-parts.

sentences.zh: 宮調之變徵、變宮在首音四音，是首音至二音，四音至五音，為半分。

translations.literal: Gong mode's altered zhi and altered gong fall on the first and fourth tones—thus from the first to the second tone, and from the fourth to the fifth, are half parts.
translations.idiomatic: In tonic mode, altered fourth and altered leading tone fall on the root and fourth degrees—so the first-to-second and fourth-to-fifth spans are half parts.

sentences.zh: 清宮調之角，變徵變宮在二音、五音，是又二音至三音，五音至六音，為半分也。

translations.literal: Raised-gong mode's jue has altered zhi and altered gong on the second and fifth tones—thus again from the second to the third tone, and from the fifth to the sixth, are half parts.
translations.idiomatic: In raised-tonic mode's third string, altered fourth and altered leading tone fall on the second and fifth degrees—again making the second-to-third and fifth-to-sixth spans half parts.

sentences.zh: 今全弦轉為徵，則三音至四音，七音至八音，為半分。

translations.literal: Now when the full string shifts to zhi, from the third to the fourth tone, and from the seventh to the eighth, are half parts.
translations.idiomatic: Retuned as fifth, the third-to-fourth and seventh-to-eighth spans become half parts.

sentences.zh: 爰定南呂之呂清徵高工為散聲首音，三音黃鍾至四音大呂為半分，七音夷則至八音南呂為半分，此弦音定陽律七調旋相為用之法也。

translations.literal: Here Nanlü yin-pipe's raised zhi "gong" is fixed as the open-string first tone; from the third tone Huangzhong to the fourth Dalü is a half part, and from the seventh Yize to the eighth Nanlü is a half part—this is the method by which string tones fix the seven yang-pipe modes to cycle and serve one another.
translations.idiomatic: Nanlü raised fifth "gong" is set as the open root; Huangzhong-to-Dalü and Yize-to-Nanlü are half parts—this is how string tuning binds the seven yang-pipe modes into a rotating system.

sentences.zh: 定陰呂七調立調之羽分，亦必以陰呂為主，其各弦各分陰陽間用亦如之。

translations.literal: In fixing the yin-pipe seven modes, the yu degree-part that establishes the mode must also take yin pipes as primary; the alternating yin-yang use of each string's degree-parts follows likewise.
translations.idiomatic: For the seven yin-pipe modes, the sixth degree-part that opens each mode must likewise be anchored in yin pipes; the yin-yang alternation across strings and parts follows the same rule.

sentences.zh: 一，弦音諸調，惟宮與商徵得與律呂相和為用，宮調各弦之七聲，皆應陽律一均。

translations.literal: First: among string-tone modes, only gong, shang, and zhi can harmonize with pitch pipes for use; gong mode's seven tones on each string all correspond to one yang-pipe octave.
translations.idiomatic: First: of all string modes, only tonic, second, and fifth can fully harmonize with the pitch-pipe system; in tonic mode, every string's seven tones answer to one yang-pipe octave.

sentences.zh: 二變七聲之分亦然。

translations.literal: The degree-parts of the two altered tones and seven tones follow likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The same holds for the two altered tones and their seven-tone degree-parts.

sentences.zh: 清宮調各弦七聲及二變七聲之分，皆應陰呂一均，此弦音宮調所以得與律呂相和。

translations.literal: Raised-gong mode's seven tones on each string and the degree-parts of the two altered seven tones all correspond to one yin-pipe octave—this is why string-tone gong mode can harmonize with pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Raised-tonic mode's seven tones on every string, including the two altered tones, all answer to one yin-pipe octave—this is how string tonic mode achieves full pitch-pipe harmony.

sentences.zh: 商調各弦之五正聲，皆應陽律，惟二變聲轉陰呂，清商調亦惟二變雜入陽律，此商調五正聲所以得與律呂相和。

translations.literal: Shang mode's five standard tones on each string all correspond to yang pitch-pipes; only the two altered tones shift to yin pipes; raised-shang mode likewise has only the two altered tones mixed into yang pipes—this is why shang mode's five standard tones can harmonize with pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: In second mode, each string's five standard tones answer to yang pipes; only the two altered tones borrow yin pipes; raised-second mode similarly mixes only its altered tones into yang pipes—hence second mode's five standard tones can harmonize with the pitch-pipe system.

sentences.zh: 徵調各弦之五正聲變宮聲皆應陽律，惟變徵一聲取陰呂，清徵調亦惟變徵一聲雜入陽律，此又徵調五正聲變宮聲得與律呂相和也。

translations.literal: Zhi mode's five standard tones and altered-gong tone on each string all correspond to yang pitch-pipes; only the altered-zhi tone takes a yin pipe; raised-zhi mode likewise has only the altered-zhi tone mixed into yang pipes—this too is why zhi mode's five standard tones and altered-gong tone can harmonize with pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: In fifth mode, each string's five standard tones and altered leading tone answer to yang pipes; only altered fourth borrows a yin pipe; raised-fifth mode similarly mixes only altered fourth into yang pipes—hence fifth mode's five standard tones and altered leading tone can harmonize with the pitch-pipe system.

sentences.zh: 至角調五正聲內，徵弦、宮弦、商弦皆應陰呂，而二變反得陽律。

translations.literal: As for jue mode's five standard tones, the zhi, gong, and shang strings all correspond to yin pipes, while the two altered tones inversely obtain yang pitch-pipes.
translations.idiomatic: In third mode's five standard tones, the fifth, tonic, and second strings answer to yin pipes, while the two altered tones borrow yang pipes instead.

sentences.zh: 且商聲乙字、羽聲凡字，各弦各分皆不得用，遺此二聲字與宮調同，清角聲五聲二變陰陽相雜亦然。

translations.literal: Moreover, shang tone's "yi" character and yu tone's "fan" character cannot be used on any string or degree-part; omitting these two note characters matches gong mode; raised jue mode's five tones and two altered tones likewise mix yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the second's "yi" and sixth's "fan" notes are unavailable on every string and part—leaving these two out as in tonic mode; raised-third mode's five tones and two altered tones similarly mix yin and yang pipes.

sentences.zh: 是角調不可與律呂相和，變徵調五正聲內宮弦應陰呂，二變亦得陽律，羽聲凡字各弦各分皆不得用，清變徵調亦宮弦雜入陽律，是變徵調不可與律呂相和，然祗借一音，即與宮調聲字為同，較角調則為正也。

translations.literal: Therefore jue mode cannot harmonize with pitch pipes; within altered-zhi mode's five standard tones the gong string corresponds to yin pipes, the two altered tones also obtain yang pitch-pipes, yu tone's "fan" character cannot be used on any string or degree-part, and raised altered-zhi mode likewise has the gong string mixed into yang pipes—therefore altered-zhi mode cannot harmonize with pitch pipes; yet borrowing only one tone, its note characters match gong mode, and compared with jue mode it is the more correct.
translations.idiomatic: Thus third mode cannot harmonize with the pitch-pipe system; in altered-fourth mode's five standard tones the tonic string answers to yin pipes while the altered tones borrow yang pipes, the sixth's "fan" is unavailable everywhere, and raised altered-fourth mode likewise mixes its tonic string into yang pipes—so altered-fourth mode too cannot fully harmonize; yet by borrowing only one tone its note characters align with tonic mode, making it sounder than third mode.

sentences.zh: 羽調五正聲內角弦應陰呂，二變應陰呂，清羽調角弦二變應陽律，是雖不可與律呂相和，然據弦音猶為七聲俱備之一調。

translations.literal: Within yu mode's five standard tones the jue string corresponds to yin pipes, the two altered tones to yin pipes; raised-yu mode's jue string and two altered tones correspond to yang pitch-pipes—thus although it cannot harmonize with pitch pipes, judged by string tones it remains one mode with all seven tones complete.
translations.idiomatic: In sixth mode's five standard tones the third string answers to yin pipes and both altered tones to yin pipes; raised-sixth mode's third string and altered tones answer to yang pipes—so though it cannot fully harmonize with the pitch-pipe system, as a string mode it still possesses all seven tones.

sentences.zh: 變宮調五正聲內徵弦宮弦皆應陰呂，而二變反得陽律。

translations.literal: Within altered-gong mode's five standard tones, the zhi and gong strings all correspond to yin pipes, while the two altered tones inversely obtain yang pitch-pipes.
translations.idiomatic: In altered-leading-tone mode's five standard tones, the fifth and tonic strings answer to yin pipes, while the two altered tones borrow yang pipes instead.

sentences.zh: 且商聲乙字、羽聲凡字，各弦各分皆不得用，遺此二聲字與角調同，清變宮五聲二變陰陽相雜亦然，是亦不可與律呂相和也。

translations.literal: Moreover, shang tone's "yi" character and yu tone's "fan" character cannot be used on any string or degree-part; omitting these two note characters matches jue mode; raised altered-gong mode's five tones and two altered tones likewise mix yin and yang—this too cannot harmonize with pitch pipes.
