sentences.zh: 右弦音旋宮轉調，就琴弦立論，以羽弦起調為主，故旋宮首徵黃鍾定二弦羽位為宮調。

translations.literal: The string-tone circular transposition and mode-shifting described above, treating the qin strings as the basis, takes the yu string as the primary opening mode; therefore in circular transposition the first mark is Huangzhong, fixing the second string's yu position as gong mode.
translations.idiomatic: The string transpositions and mode shifts above are framed from the qin strings themselves, with the sixth string as the primary opening tone; thus in the rotating system Huangzhong is first marked by fixing the second string's sixth position as tonic mode.

sentences.zh: 律呂后編以七音立論，立宮為主，黃鍾為宮，則弦之宮分聲應黃鍾，商分應太簇，角分應姑洗，變徵分應蕤賓，徵分應夷則，羽分應無射，變宮分應半黃鍾。

translations.literal: The pitch-pipe section that follows argues from the seven tones, taking gong as primary: when Huangzhong is gong, the string's gong degree-part answers to Huangzhong, the shang part to Taicu, the jue part to Guxian, the altered-zhi part to Ruibin, the zhi part to Yize, the yu part to Wushe, and the altered-gong part to half Huangzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The lü section below adopts the seven-tone framework with tonic as foundation: when Huangzhong serves as tonic, the string's tonic part answers to Huangzhong, the second to Taicu, the third to Guxian, altered fourth to Ruibin, fifth to Yize, sixth to Wushe, and altered leading tone to half Huangzhong.

sentences.zh: 即倍無射。

translations.literal: That is, doubled Wushe.
translations.idiomatic: That is, doubled Wushe.

sentences.zh: 大呂為宮，七音之分應陰呂亦然。

translations.literal: When Dalü is gong, the degree-parts of the seven tones likewise answer to yin pipes.
translations.idiomatic: When Dalü serves as tonic, the seven tone degree-parts answer to yin pipes in the same way.

sentences.zh: 以分言，則宮分應黃鍾者即黃鍾之分，商分即太簇之分，角分即姑洗之分，變徵分即蕤賓之分。

translations.literal: Stated in terms of degree-parts, the gong part answering to Huangzhong is simply the Huangzhong part, the shang part the Taicu part, the jue part the Guxian part, and the altered-zhi part the Ruibin part.
translations.idiomatic: In terms of degree-parts alone, the tonic part answering to Huangzhong is the Huangzhong part, the second the Taicu part, the third the Guxian part, and the altered fourth the Ruibin part.

sentences.zh: 至徵分應夷則者，則非夷則之分，而為林鍾之分。

translations.literal: But as for the zhi part answering to Yize, it is not the Yize part but the Linzhong part.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the fifth part that answers to Yize is not the Yize part but the Linzhong part.

sentences.zh: 羽分應無射者，亦非無射之分，而為南呂之分。

translations.literal: The yu part answering to Wushe is likewise not the Wushe part but the Nanlü part.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth part answering to Wushe is likewise not the Wushe part but the Nanlü part.

sentences.zh: 變宮分應半黃鍾者，非半黃鍾之分，而為應鍾之分。

translations.literal: The altered-gong part answering to half Huangzhong is not the half-Huangzhong part but the Yingzhong part.
translations.idiomatic: The altered leading-tone part answering to half Huangzhong is not the half-Huangzhong part but the Yingzhong part.

sentences.zh: 大呂為宮，變徵分則為變林鍾之分，徵分則為夷則之分，羽分則為無射之分，變宮分則為變黃鍾之分。

translations.literal: When Dalü is gong, the altered-zhi part becomes the altered-Linzhong part, the zhi part the Yize part, the yu part the Wushe part, and the altered-gong part the altered-Huangzhong part.
translations.idiomatic: When Dalü serves as tonic, the altered-fourth part becomes the altered Linzhong part, the fifth the Yize part, the sixth the Wushe part, and the altered leading tone the altered Huangzhong part.

sentences.zh: 其陰陽各七均，均各七弦，有表詳樂問，不備載。

translations.literal: Yin and yang each have seven octaves, and each octave has seven strings; tables in Le Wen treat this in detail, and it is not fully reproduced here.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and yang each comprise seven octaves, and each octave seven strings; the tables in Le Wen give full detail, which is not reproduced here.

sentences.zh: 二倍加四分之一黃鍾之管夷則徵聲乙字黃鍾八分之二又加此一分之四分之一之管

translations.literal: Pipe of two times Huangzhong plus one-quarter: Yize zhi tone, yi character—the pipe of two-eighths of Huangzhong plus one-quarter of that two-eighths.
translations.idiomatic: The pipe two times Huangzhong plus one-quarter yields the Yize fifth (zhi), notated yi—the pipe at two-eighths of Huangzhong plus one-quarter of that fraction.
